title: Anoscopy and rectoscopy
what: The doctor looks at the anus and rectum using a small tube with a light. It is a short exam, usually without anesthesia.
why: For blood in the stool, pain or itching around the anus, hemorrhoids, a tear, or before surgery.
tell_doctor: If you have severe pain around the anus right now
If you had surgery in this area before

prepare.title: Bowel
prepare.text: Usually the bowel needs to be cleaned: an enema or mini-enema in the evening and in the morning. Your clinic will tell you how.

prepare.title: Anoscopy only
prepare.text: For a short exam of the anus, a normal bowel movement in the morning is sometimes enough. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light dinner the evening before. In the morning, a light breakfast is fine, unless your clinic says otherwise.

bring: Past reports, if you have them
steps: You lie on your left side with your knees pulled up, or kneel on your knees and elbows
The doctor first looks at the area and gently checks with a finger
A tube with gel on it is put in a short way
The doctor looks at the bowel walls and takes the tube out
feel: Pressure and a feeling that you need the toilet. This is normal
During rectoscopy, a little air is put into the bowel, so you may feel bloated
If it hurts, tell the doctor
after: You can eat and go about your day right away
A little blood on the toilet paper the same day can happen, especially if a tissue sample was taken
The doctor usually tells you the results right away
red_flags: Severe belly pain, or fever above 38 degrees

faq.a: Usually not. It is uncomfortable but bearable. If you have a tear, the doctor uses a numbing gel.

faq.q: How is rectoscopy different from colonoscopy?
faq.a: Rectoscopy looks only at the rectum and the start of the sigmoid colon. Colonoscopy looks at the whole large bowel.

reminders.text: Rectal exam tomorrow. Tonight, clean your bowel as your clinic said, and have a light dinner.
This morning, clean your bowel as your clinic planned. Bring your referral and list of medicines.
